findings.summary: Soundness: the coverage rule throws away the bullet words that the request's prose repeats, then judges coverage on the incidental words left over. As a result it wrongly refuses readings that cover every bullet, and it catches the motivating case only through an accident of word forms.
findings.evidence: I ran the candidate's check-reading on both readings the replay newly refused. ttnw is refused for 'a test: with no improvement requests queued, ordering is unchanged', yet its criterion says 'a new test with no Steward or Hestia requests queued asserts the plan order is identical to the order before the change'. bp5e is refused for 'The root cause is named in the change description…', yet its criterion says 'its doc comment names the root cause'. Both jobs' verification.json record request_reading_mismatch: null. After removing prose words, the only word left to judge was 'unchanged' for ttnw and 'description' for bp5e, and the criteria lacked it. The sza7 refusal also rests on one leftover word, 'flags', because the prose says 'flagged' and the two forms reduce to different stems ('flag', 'flagg'); this is from reading the code, not a run. Had the bullet said 'flagged', the rule would fall back to the bullet's other unique words, 'duration' would match criterion 4's 'measured duration', and the omission would be accepted. So 2 of the 2 replayed refusals are wrong, and the true catch is fragile. A better alternative: score each bullet against its best-matching criterion by the share of the bullet's own content words found there, without removing prose words, and tune the threshold on the replay set so that ttnw and bp5e are accepted and sza7 is refused.

findings.summary: Two changed files are outside the expected deliverables: crates/athena-agent/src/fake.rs and crates/athena-cli/tests/drain.rs.
findings.evidence: git diff HEAD~1 --stat lists both, and neither is on the deliverables list. The fake reader now repeats the request's bullets in its criterion, and the drain test helper appends '- the tests still pass' to steward requests. Both look necessary to keep the suite passing under the new rule. The reading said no consumers existed, so this was missed when the reading was made.

findings.evidence: The plan said the probe would use this job's own reading criteria 1 to 8. The case uses 5 different, hand-written criteria. I checked the real reading separately with check-reading on this job's reading-1.json, and it returned 'accept'.

summary: I judged the candidate on what I read and ran. Every acceptance criterion is met: the new check is one step! line in refusing_check, its tests and the 15 corpus cases pass, the doc and CHANGELOG say what was asked, and Athena's recorded fmt, clippy and test runs passed. I also ran the candidate's `athena check-reading` on real records in the evidence snapshot. It refuses the reading of the 2026-10-29 job that caused this request (20261029-084645-sza7) and accepts this job's own reading. The verdict is still fail, because the matching rule is unsound. Its two refusals in the replay, 20261107-031902-ttnw and 20261109-161505-bp5e, are both wrong.
